questions.question: Compare the role of symmetric encryption and asymmetric encryption / in SSL.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the role of symmetric encryption and asymmetric
  • encryption
  • Symmetric encryption uses a single shared key for both encryption
  • and decryption.
  • Asymmetric encryption uses a pair of keys — a public key for
  • encryption and a private key for decryption.
questions.final_answer: encryption and a private key for decryption

questions.question: Examine how TLS protects against common security threats.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine how TLS protects against common security threats.
  • TLS protects against threats like eavesdropping, tampering, and
  • message forgery by providing encryption, message integrity, and
  • authentication between communicating parties.

questions.question: Explain the term access control policy.
questions.solution_html:
• Access control policy defines who (users or processes) can access
  • what resources and under what conditions. It ensures
  • confidentiality, integrity, and availability by restricting
  • unauthorized access.Policies are based on principles like least
  • privilege and need-to-know.Common types include Discretionary
  • Access Control (DAC), Mandatory Access Control (MAC), and
  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
  • Explanation, common types etc – (5 marks)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Distinguish between authentication and authorization.
questions.solution_html:
• Authentication verifies the identity of a user or system (e.g., via
  • password, biometrics).
  • Authorization determines the permissions or access rights granted
  • to an authenticated user.
  • Definition ,purpose, example etc – (5 marks)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss about the different types of phishing.
questions.solution_html:
• Email Phishing: Fake emails trick users into revealing personal or
  • financial data.
  • Spear Phishing: Targeted phishing aimed at specific individuals
  • or organizations.
  • Whaling: Phishing attacks directed at high-profile targets like
  • executives.
  • Smishing: Phishing through SMS messages.
  • Vishing: Voice-based phishing attacks via phone calls pretending
  • to be legitimate sources.
  • Explanation of different types -(5 marks)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write the uses of tunneling protocols in VPN
questions.solution_html:
• Tunneling protocols encapsulate data packets to create a secure
  • communication channel over public networks. Provide data
  • confidentiality through encryption during transmission. Ensure data
  • integrity and authentication of communicating parties. Common
  • VPN tunneling protocols: PPTP, L2TP, IPsec, SSL/TLS, and
  • OpenVPN. Used for remote access, secure communication, and
  • bypassing geographic or network restrictions.
  • Explanation – (5 marks)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how encryption protects mobile apps.
questions.solution_html:
• Encryption converts sensitive app data into unreadable form
  • protecting it from unauthorized access. Safeguards stored data (at
  • rest) and transmitted data (in transit). Prevents data leakage if a
  • device is lost or compromised. Protects communications between
  • app and server using SSL/TLS encryption. Ensures compliance
  • with security standards and user privacy protection.
  • Explanation – (5 marks)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Illustrate the dangers of weak cryptography in web applications.
questions.solution_html:
• applications.
  • Weak cryptography can be easily broken, leading to data breaches
  • and unauthorized access. Enables attackers to decrypt sensitive
  • information like passwords or financial data. Makes web
  • applications vulnerable to man-in-the-middle (MITM) and replay
  • attacks. Affects user trust and may lead to legal and reputational
  • damage. Using strong, modern algorithms (e.g., AES, SHA-256)
  • helps prevent such vulnerabilities
  • Explanaton – (5 marks)
  • (4*5=20)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

  • SQL Injection, Insider Threats, Spyware and Adware, Password
  • Attacks, Zero-Day Exploits, Social Engineering
  • Explanation of any 7 – (10 marks)

  • Authentication Header Provides authentication and integrity for IP

questions.solution_html:

  • IT Network Access, resources are hosted locally on-premises
  • within the organization’s own infrastructure.
